items.text: A person becomes an artist. The best explanation is:

options.A: They're the artistic type—it's their nature (formism)
options.C: Their whole self developed toward this expression (organicism)
options.D: Unique confluence of factors in their particular situation (contextualism)
options.E: No single framework captures it—need multiple approaches

items.text: To understand why something happened, it's most useful to ask:

options.A: What category or type does this belong to?
options.B: What were the causes and mechanisms?
options.C: What larger pattern or whole was emerging?
options.D: What was unique about this particular situation?
options.E: Depends on what you're trying to understand

options.A: Things act according to their nature and type
options.B: Prior causes determined them through causal chains
options.C: They emerged from developing wholes seeking completion
options.D: Unique circumstances came together in particular ways
options.E: Multiple frameworks are needed—no single answer suffices
